items.q: Match each cast with its association — 1) RBC cast 2) WBC cast 3) Fatty cast … A) Lipiduria (nephrotic syndrome), Fabry's B) Glomerular hematuria C) Acute pyelonephritis, PSGN, ATN/AIN
items.exp: RBC cast – glomerular hematuria; WBC cast – acute pyelonephritis, PSGN, ATN/AIN; fatty cast – lipiduria, Fabry's. (Book p746)

items.q: Pigment fine granular casts point to pigment nephropathy caused by:
items.exp: Pigment fine granular cast: pigment nephropathy – hemolysis; rhabdomyolysis. (Book p746)

items.q: The cast described as most specific for ATN/AIN is the:
items.exp: Tubular epithelial cast (muddy brown): ATN/AIN (most specific). (Book p746)

items.q: Broad casts and waxy casts are the markers of:
items.exp: Broad cast and waxy cast: chronic kidney disease. (Book p746)

items.q: Fractured casts, seen on biopsy, are associated with:
A patient with drug-induced interstitial injury shows casts packed with eosinophils. The association listed is:
Pigment nephropathy with pigment fine granular casts arises from all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: Pigment nephropathy: hemolysis, rhabdomyolysis; nephrotic syndrome instead gives fatty casts/lipiduria. (Book p746)

items.q: Fill up: The muddy brown cast of ATN/AIN is a ______ cast.
items.exp: Tubular epithelial cast (muddy brown): ATN/AIN (most specific). (Book p746)

items.q: Which cast statement is TRUE as per the table?
opts: WBC casts occur in acute pyelonephritis, post-streptococcal GN and ATN/AIN
WBC casts are specific for chronic kidney disease
items.exp: WBC cast: acute pyelonephritis; PSGN; ATN/AIN. RBC cast = glomerular hematuria; waxy = CKD. (Book p746)

items.q: Match each cast with its association — 1) Broad & waxy casts 2) Fractured cast (on biopsy) 3) Eosinophil cast … A) ATN/AIN B) Myeloma C) Chronic kidney disease
items.exp: Broad/waxy – CKD; fractured – myeloma; eosinophil – ATN/AIN. (Book p746)
Fatty cast: lipiduria (nephrotic syndrome); Fabry's. (Book p746)
